newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - BZW favours software firms.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - BZW favours software firms.

text.p: Barclays de Zoete Wedd said on Thursday new business generated by the "millennium bug" and the European single currency will boost software companies like Cap Gemini Sogetti, Logica Plc and Sligos.
BZW, in a media presentation, said annual sales in the European software market would be boosted by between five and 10 per cent over the next three years.
Profit margins will also be enhanced, BZW said.
BZW said that profit margins in the European software industry now range from six to 15 per cent.
Companies like Logica with profit margins at the low point of the range should be able to improve to at least 10 per cent, BZW said.
BZW said it estimated the cost of creating Millennium compliant software systems for European companies would be around $15.7 billion, of which 40 per cent would be outsourced to software companies.
"Of this ($6.3 billion) we expect 50 per cent actually to be additional turnover. The remainder is likely to be funded from existing budgets," BZW said in the report.
The BZW report said the change to the "euro" will be four times more expensive than the Millennium bug issue.

"We believe its (the euro's) impact is four times greater for the software industry than the Year 2000 issue. Total costs are estimated at $25.3 billion of which 50 per cent is likely to be outsourced."
"In this case, however, the work will be additional to existing IT (Information Technology) budgets," the BZW report said.
Some companies would benefit to a greater extent than others, and BZW ranked them in order of exposure to the issues.
- Axime and Sligos, which have proposed a merger. BZW said they have greater exposure to banking, and therefore expect more impact from the euro.
- Cap Gemini SA, and its Netherlands quoted subsidiary Cap Gemini NV.
- Getronics, a full service supplier in the Netherlands.
